text: Moat or niche comes down to where Juniper Cola's audience sits among the brands it shares taste with, and whether that position is its own.
The opening scan is already mapping Juniper Cola against five peers, so I will not repeat it. Writing the priors first, before any data comes back.
My expectation: it competes with Foxglove Cola and Harbor Seltzer, it sits near the centre of soft drinks, and its taste is fairly distinctive. A second home outside beverages would surprise me.
Resolving Foxglove Cola and Harbor Seltzer now, so step S3 can score them against Juniper Cola once the scan is back.

draft.headline: Juniper Cola is a taste island: its closest audience is an apparel brand
draft.thesis: Juniper Cola sits apart from the soft drinks around it ({{M12}}) and has the lowest hub score in its map ({{M10}}) [E3]: its peers share their audiences with each other first. Its closest match is Granite Outfitters, an apparel brand, at {{M11}}, and its taste is the most distinct in the map ({{M9}}). A niche with a distinct taste, not yet a moat: Granite Outfitters' own map scores Juniper Cola at {{M53}}, behind Kettle Denim and Pinecone Outfitters [E10].

hypothesis_verdicts.note: Foxglove Cola scores {{M43}} with Juniper Cola and Harbor Seltzer {{M41}}, both below Granite Outfitters at {{M11}}.
Juniper Cola sits at the edge of its category ({{M12}}) and has the lowest hub score in the map ({{M10}}): its peers look to each other first.
Juniper Cola has the most distinct taste in the map ({{M9}}).

Juniper Cola's closest match is Granite Outfitters at {{M11}}, but not the other way round: Granite Outfitters' own map scores Juniper Cola at {{M53}}, behind Kettle Denim ({{M47}}) and Pinecone Outfitters ({{M51}}).

arguments.qloo_fact: Juniper Cola sits apart from its peers ({{M12}}) [E3], and its hub score is the lowest in the map ({{M10}}).
arguments.our_read: The colas and seltzers around it share their audiences with each other first; Juniper Cola is not part of that exchange.

arguments.qloo_fact: Juniper Cola's closest match is Granite Outfitters at {{M11}} [E3], found by cross-category discovery [E1]. Scored in one set of calls, Foxglove Cola reaches {{M43}} and Harbor Seltzer {{M41}} [E9].
arguments.our_read: The audience's cultural home sits outside beverages, nearer an apparel brand than the colas it shelves next to.

arguments.qloo_fact: Granite Outfitters' own map scores Juniper Cola at {{M53}}, behind Kettle Denim ({{M47}}) and Pinecone Outfitters ({{M51}}) [E10]; its hub score there sits in the lower half ({{M54}}).
arguments.our_read: The pull runs from Juniper Cola toward Granite Outfitters, not back. A partnership would borrow that brand's audience rather than share one.

arguments.qloo_fact: Juniper Cola has the most distinct taste in the map ({{M9}}) [E3].
arguments.our_read: A distinct taste is the raw material of a moat. Without peers that share it, it is also what a niche looks like.

limitations.text: Some Qloo responses were served from an older cached copy because a fresh call failed; their fetch times show their real age.
Age and gender figures are relative affinity indices, not population shares, and gender is binary in the source.
Entities tied at a context's floor score show no measurable relationship to that signal, so they are not scored there, never ranked.
Taste signals describe audience affinity, not revenue, market share or valuation.
Peer similarity is audience taste similarity, not switching, share or sales.
A snapshot of Qloo's taste graph at fetch time; it holds no prices, filings or sales data.
Only exact name and type matches are used; close candidates are offered, never applied.
Each row comes from a single seed, and scores are compressed, so ranks are read rather than raw scores.
Entities without a score are shown as not measured.
Facet tags are qualitative descriptors from Qloo's entity tags, not survey answers.
Only Qloo's top US destinations for this audience are compared.
Travel taste shows places this audience's taste points to, not residence, trips taken or ticket demand.
Does the island hold in each metro, or only nationally?

disclaimers: Aggregated group-level taste signals; no individual-level inference.
Data: synthetic sample from the mock Qloo transport and a scripted model; no Qloo or model calls were made, and the model spend shown is scripted.
